content.user_title: Render Math in Obsidian with MathJax
content.value_statement: Writing reliable mathematical notation in Obsidian requires precise MathJax syntax. This skill supplies practical patterns and a detailed reference for common formulas.
actual_capabilities: Formats inline and block mathematical expressions for Obsidian MathJax.
Produces fractions, roots, scripts, Greek letters, relations, and operators.
Builds matrices, aligned equations, and conditional definitions.
Writes integrals, sums, products, limits, and scalable delimiters.
Applies mathematical fonts, accents, arrows, and spacing commands.
Uses a local reference containing extended symbols and environments.
limitations: The skill does not render or visually test equations inside Obsidian.
It does not validate whether a mathematical statement is correct.
Package-specific LaTeX commands may not be supported by Obsidian MathJax.
The skill provides syntax guidance and does not modify a vault by itself.

use_cases.title: Prepare Study Notes
use_cases.description: Convert handwritten formulas into readable inline or block expressions for an Obsidian course notebook.

use_cases.title: Document Technical Results
use_cases.description: Format matrices, derivations, integrals, and probability expressions for research notes.

use_cases.title: Standardize Knowledge Bases
use_cases.description: Apply consistent notation, spacing, and equation structure across shared technical documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Format a Basic Formula
prompt_templates.prompt: Format [formula] for Obsidian. Use inline MathJax when compact, or a block when the expression needs emphasis.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a first MathJax expression from a plain-language formula.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these rows into an Obsidian MathJax matrix: [rows]. Use [parentheses, brackets, or determinant bars].
prompt_templates.scenario: Build a structured matrix with the requested delimiters.

prompt_templates.title: Align a Derivation
prompt_templates.prompt: Format this derivation as aligned Obsidian MathJax: [steps]. Align each equality and preserve explanatory text.
prompt_templates.scenario: Present a multi-step calculation with consistent alignment.

prompt_templates.title: Compose Advanced Technical Notation
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite [technical passage] with Obsidian-compatible MathJax. Include appropriate matrices, cases, operators, delimiters, fonts, accents, and spacing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Standardize complex mathematical notation in a technical note.

output_examples.input: Format the quadratic formula as a centered equation for Obsidian.
output_examples.output: A centered MathJax block displaying x = (-b plus or minus the square root of b squared minus 4ac) divided by 2a.

output_examples.input: Show a two-row identity matrix with square brackets.
output_examples.output: A square-bracketed two by two matrix with ones on the diagonal and zeros elsewhere.

output_examples.input: Present two expansion steps for the square of a plus b.
output_examples.output: An aligned block showing the product expansion first, followed by the simplified polynomial on the next line.

best_practices: Use inline delimiters for short expressions and block delimiters for prominent or multiline equations.
Wrap multi-character scripts in braces and use explicit spacing where notation requires it.
Choose matrix environments and scalable delimiters that match the mathematical meaning.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every desktop LaTeX package command works in Obsidian MathJax.
Do not place long derivations inline when a structured aligned block is clearer.
Do not omit braces around multi-character superscripts or subscripts.

faq.question: Does this skill install MathJax?
faq.answer: No. Obsidian already uses MathJax, and this skill provides compatible syntax guidance.

faq.question: Can it create inline and block equations?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains both forms and selects a form based on expression length and context.

faq.question: Does it support matrices?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers plain, parenthesized, bracketed, determinant, norm, and small matrix environments.

faq.question: Can it format aligned derivations and cases?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents alignment points, line breaks, explanatory text, and conditional definitions.

faq.question: Does it verify mathematical correctness?
faq.answer: No. Review the underlying mathematics separately from the MathJax formatting.

faq.question: Where are less common symbols documented?
faq.answer: The included reference lists extended symbols, operators, arrows, delimiters, fonts, accents, functions, and environments.
